territorial_scope.description: Federal executive order addressed to federal agencies; covers federal lands and projects, and under Sec. 7(a) permitting on Federal and non-Federal lands.

evidence.quote: By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered:

summary.short: Executive Order of July 23, 2025 directs federal agencies to speed permitting, NEPA and ESA review, financial support and federal-land access for AI data centers above 100 MW and related covered components such as energy infrastructure and semiconductors.
summary.long: Directs federal agencies to speed permitting and support for Qualifying Projects: AI data centers over 100 MW of new load and related Covered Components, including energy infrastructure, natural gas turbines, semiconductors and data storage. Sec. 2 defines Qualifying Projects by capital expenditure of at least $500 million, incremental load above 100 MW, national-security status, or designation by a named Secretary. Sec. 3 directs Commerce to launch a financial support initiative (loans, guarantees, grants, tax incentives, offtake agreements). Sec. 4 revokes Executive Order 14141. Sec. 5 has agencies identify categorical exclusions under NEPA and CEQ coordinate new ones; federal financial assistance below 50% of project cost is presumed not substantial federal control. Sec. 6 lets the FPISC Executive Director designate transparency projects and publish them on the Permitting Dashboard. Sec. 7 directs EPA to expedite permitting and identify Brownfield and Superfund sites, with guidance within 180 days. Sec. 8 requires programmatic ESA consultation and an Army review of nationwide permits within 180 days. Sec. 9 directs Interior and Energy to offer authorizations on federal sites and Defense to identify and lease military-installation sites. Sec. 10 disclaims enforceable rights and makes implementation subject to law and appropriations.

notes: Text as signed on July 23, 2025; no Federal Register citation or consolidated version is given. Sec. 4 revokes EO 14141 but does not say which of its provisions, if any, continue. The 100 MW figure appears in Sec. 2(a) (new dedicated AI load) and Sec. 2(d)(ii) (incremental load addition), with different measures. 'Protects national security' in Sec. 2(d)(iii) is not defined. Sec. 6(a) makes designation discretionary ('may'), while Sec. 6(b) uses 'shall expedite'. Sec. 10(b) makes implementation subject to applicable law and appropriations; Sec. 10(c) states no enforceable rights are created. The text contains no penalty or enforcement provisions. Statutory references are cited as written; several (e.g., 42 U.S.C. 2201, 42 U.S.C. 7256) are not coded as relations.

enforcement.note: The order directs federal agencies to take permitting, financing, environmental-review and land-availability actions (Secs. 3, 5-9) and sets up no fines, penalties, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking. Sec. 10(c) states the order creates no right enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States or any other person.
